quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

36 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: What is the difference between a red arrow traffic light and a solid red light?

options.text: Red arrows only stop traffic that is turning.
Red arrows are only used in protected turn lanes.
You cannot turn on a red arrow, even if you stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn on a red arrow, even if you stop first.
questions.explanation: You can sometimes turn right at a solid red light after stopping. You can never turn left or right at a red arrow, even after stopping.

questions.question: A safety zone is a marked area where passengers board or leave buses or trolleys. You cannot drive through a safety zone:

options.text: When a bus or trolley is there.
When a bus or trolley is dropping off passengers.
At any time, for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: At any time, for any reason.
questions.explanation: You can never drive through a safety zone. This space is reserved for pedestrians.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must drive through the intersection at the posted speed limit.
The maximum speed limit is 55 mph under good conditions.
You must not drive below the posted speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum speed limit is 55 mph under good conditions.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the maximum speed limit for this road. You can drive slower than the posted limit based on road conditions. However, it is illegal to drive faster than the posted limit.

questions.question: When driving on a road with a single broken white centerline, can you cross it?

options.text: No, you must stay in your lane.
Yes, you can cross it to change lanes.
Yes, but only if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, you can cross it to change lanes.
questions.explanation: White broken lines mean lanes go in the same direction. You can cross a broken white line to pass another vehicle when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign indicate?

options.text: There is a steep hill ahead.
Trucks are not allowed on this hill.
A logging road is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you of a steep hill ahead. Slow down and be ready to control your speed to protect your brakes.

questions.question: Which of the following causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Driving above the speed limit or driving too fast for conditions.
Getting enough rest and staying alert.
Watching your surroundings and focusing on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving above the speed limit or driving too fast for conditions.
questions.explanation: Speeding and driving too fast for conditions are common causes of accidents. Always drive within the speed limit and with the flow of traffic.

questions.question: On a multilane road, a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from the side with the dashed line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed only from the side with the dashed line.
questions.explanation: When there is a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line, only drivers next to the dashed line can cross and pass. Drivers next to the solid line cannot pass.

questions.question: To enter a gap in highway traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Only watch vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up so other vehicles will move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before you change lanes or enter traffic, check for vehicles beside and behind your car. Make sure the lane is clear before you move into it.

questions.question: When must you always stop your vehicle at a traffic light?

options.text: Solid red, flashing red, and broken traffic signals.
Solid red, red arrows, and flashing yellow.
Solid red, flashing red, and yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Solid red, flashing red, and broken traffic signals.
questions.explanation: You must stop at solid or flashing red lights, or at broken signals. A solid yellow light means the light is about to turn red—stop if you can do so safely. A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution, but you do not need to stop.

questions.question: What should a driver do about right-of-way rules?

options.text: Assume all drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to give up your right-of-way if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to give up your right-of-way if needed.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you automatically have the right-of-way. Always consider the situation at an intersection. Be willing to yield your right-of-way to prevent a collision.

questions.question: When passing a row of parked vehicles, you should:

options.text: Be ready for a person or vehicle to move into your lane without warning.
Expect all drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.
Drive close to parked vehicles to leave room for moving traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or vehicle to move into your lane without warning.
questions.explanation: Keep distance between your car and parked vehicles. A person may step out of a parked car or from between cars. A driver may start moving their car before seeing you.

questions.question: When can you drive in a bicycle lane?

options.text: When you need the space and the bike lane is empty.
When passing another vehicle.
When parking (where allowed), entering or leaving the road, or turning (within 200 feet of an intersection).

questions.correctAnswerText: When parking (where allowed), entering or leaving the road, or turning (within 200 feet of an intersection).
questions.explanation: You can only drive in a bicycle lane when parking (where allowed), entering or leaving the road, or turning (within 200 feet of an intersection).

questions.question: When you see a person crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until the person is far away from your path.
Honk your horn as you pass them.
Carefully drive around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is far away from your path.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind person using a white cane or guide dog crossing the street, you must stop. Wait until they are completely clear of your path. Always give blind pedestrians the right-of-way.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the lap belt.
Use both the lap belt and shoulder belt.
Use only the shoulder belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap belt and shoulder belt.
questions.explanation: Use both parts of your seat belt. Using only one part does not protect you as well. Even if you have an automatic shoulder belt, fasten your lap belt too.

questions.question: Remove snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield.
All windows.
Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: All windows.
questions.explanation: You need to see clearly through all your vehicle's windows before driving. Remove snow, ice, and frost from all windows and mirrors before you start driving.

questions.question: Can you drive off the road to pass another vehicle?

options.text: Yes, if the vehicle ahead is turning left.
Yes, if there are two or more lanes going your direction.
No, under no circumstances.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, under no circumstances.
questions.explanation: You can never drive off the road onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: Why should you increase your following distance behind a large vehicle?

options.text: To see around the sides of the vehicle better.
Because other drivers tend to cut in before passing large vehicles.
Because following too closely will pull your vehicle along with theirs.

questions.correctAnswerText: To see around the sides of the vehicle better.
questions.explanation: Truck, bus, and van drivers may not see you if you are directly behind them. Keep extra distance so you can see around the sides and see the road ahead.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a freeway, you should:

options.text: Signal for at least five seconds.
Slow down before changing lanes.
Assume there is space in the next lane if you signal first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal for at least five seconds.
questions.explanation: Signal at least five seconds before you change lanes on a freeway. Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping so other drivers and pedestrians know what you are doing.

questions.question: You are driving on the freeway behind a large truck. How should you drive?

options.text: Drive close behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead.
Drive farther back from the truck than you would from a regular car.
Drive no more than one car length behind so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive farther back from the truck than you would from a regular car.
questions.explanation: If you drive too close behind a truck, the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. This is dangerous because you lose your safety space if the truck stops quickly.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in a residential area if no sign is posted?

options.text: 20 mph
25 mph
30 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: 25 mph
questions.explanation: The default speed limit in residential and business areas is 25 mph unless a different sign is posted.

questions.question: You hit an animal with your vehicle on a California highway. What should you do?

options.text: Move the injured animal off the road.
Call the humane society.
Keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Call the humane society.
questions.explanation: Call the California Highway Patrol, the local humane society, or police. Do not leave the animal or try to move it yourself.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield to:

options.text: Cars passing you.
Cars coming toward you.
No one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars coming toward you.
questions.explanation: You must let oncoming traffic go first. Only turn left when it is safe and you will not affect oncoming vehicles.

questions.question: When turning right from a highway with two lanes in your direction, which lane should you turn from?

options.text: The lane closest to the center of the road.
The lane nearest the curb or edge of the road.
Either lane, depending on oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane nearest the curb or edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Start and end your right turn in the right lane. Do not swing wide into another lane of traffic.

questions.question: Is it okay to block an intersection during rush hour traffic if you have a green light?

options.text: Yes, if you entered on a green light.
No, never, even with a green light.
Yes, if you have the right-of-way or a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never, even with a green light.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can drive all the way across before the light turns red. You can get a ticket for blocking an intersection.

questions.question: When you see a stop sign, what should you do?

options.text: Check only in the direction you plan to go, then proceed.
Let all other vehicles go first.
Come to a full stop and check for traffic in all directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and check for traffic in all directions.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop at a stop sign and look for traffic in all directions before proceeding.

questions.question: When is it legal to block an intersection?

options.text: If you entered on a green light.
During rush hour.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, only enter an intersection if you can drive all the way across before the light turns red. Blocking an intersection can result in a ticket.

questions.question: You want to park downhill on a road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the edge of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the edge of the road
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road when parking downhill. This way, if your brakes fail, your car will roll away from traffic. When parking uphill on a road with a curb, turn toward the center so the car rolls into the curb.

questions.question: With a Class C driver license, what vehicles can you drive?

options.text: A three-axle vehicle weighing less than 6,000 pounds.
Any three-axle vehicle, regardless of weight.
A vehicle with two trailers.

questions.correctAnswerText: A three-axle vehicle weighing less than 6,000 pounds.
questions.explanation: A Class C license allows you to drive a three-axle vehicle only if it weighs 6,000 pounds or less.

questions.question: When backing up safely, which of these is NOT required?

options.text: Look over your right shoulder as you back up.
Check your surroundings before backing.
Tap your horn before backing up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your horn before backing up.
questions.explanation: Before backing, check around your vehicle. While backing, look over your shoulder to stay aware. Tapping your horn is not required for safe backing.

questions.question: A freeway speed limit is 65 mph, but traffic is going 70 mph. What is the legal speed you can drive?

options.text: 70 mph or faster to keep up with traffic.
Between 65 and 70 mph.
No faster than 65 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: No faster than 65 mph.
questions.explanation: You must follow the posted speed limit of 65 mph. You can only drive 70 mph if that speed is posted as the limit.

questions.question: A truck or bus is turning right where you also need to turn right. What should you do?

options.text: Turn quickly before the truck or bus.
Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning.
questions.explanation: Do not try to squeeze your vehicle between a turning truck or bus and the curb. This can cause a serious crash. Wait for the truck or bus to complete its turn first.

questions.question: How should you properly make a right turn?

options.text: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the centerline before turning.
Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
Approach from the right lane, but move toward the middle of the street before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
questions.explanation: Signal your turn. Slow down. Move to the right lane and stay close to the right curb before and during your turn.

questions.question: What does a yellow pennant-shaped sign say?

options.text: Right turns only.
Right turns permitted.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: Yellow pennant-shaped signs mark no passing zones.

questions.question: When parking parallel to a curb on a level street, what must be true?

options.text: Your front wheels must face the street.
Your wheels must be within 18 inches of the curb.
One rear wheel must touch the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your wheels must be within 18 inches of the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking parallel to the curb on a level street, keep your wheels parallel to and within 18 inches of the curb.

questions.question: How can you help keep drivers behind you at a safe distance?

options.text: Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
Drive at a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at a steady speed.
questions.explanation: Maintain a steady speed and signal your turns and lane changes in advance. This helps drivers behind you stay at a safe distance.

questions.question: When driving in a construction zone, what should you do?

options.text: Slightly increase your speed.
Expect the unexpected.
Expect construction workers to yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the unexpected.
questions.explanation: Construction zones can have unexpected conditions. Drive carefully to protect yourself, other drivers, and construction workers.
